keyVerseText: Fifty loops shalt thou make in the one curtain, and fifty loops shalt thou make in the edge of the curtain that is in the coupling of the second; that the loops may take hold one of another.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb קָבַל (qâbal) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys the idea of receiving or taking hold of something. Its core sense involves admitting or accepting, whether literally taking an object or figuratively accepting a concept or responsibility. This root sense enriches the common English gloss by emphasizing an active engagement or choice to receive, rather than a passive occurrence.
usageInScripture: Throughout its thirteen occurrences, קָבַל consistently carries the sense of receiving, taking, or choosing, as reflected in translations like 'received,' 'choose,' and 'may take hold.' This range shows the word’s flexibility in describing both physical reception and more abstract acceptance or assumption. The verb also appears in forms that express mutual correspondence or opposition, highlighting relational dynamics in reception.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding קָבַל as an active reception deepens our grasp of biblical faith, where believers are called not merely to hear but to receive and embrace God’s promises and commands. This verb underscores the personal responsibility inherent in faith, illustrating that grace and truth are not forced upon us but are chosen and accepted. Christ’s invitation to receive salvation echoes this root meaning, inviting us to take hold of the new life offered in Him. Thus, קָבַל enriches our appreciation of the believer’s response in the covenant relationship with God.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 26:5 speaks of making fifty loops on each curtain edge so that 'the loops may take hold one of another.' Here, קָבַל conveys the idea of a firm, mutual reception or connection, emphasizing the strength and unity in the tabernacle’s construction. The word highlights how each part is intentionally designed to receive and hold the other, symbolizing the interconnectedness and support within God’s dwelling place among His people.
